pages.text: Place a $(item)rotor$() and surround it with $(item)8 stators$() in a ring, square around the rotor's axis: four on the sides and four on the corners. The stators take their shape by themselves. The rotor only generates when all eight are in place. Both parts come from a mechanical crafter.

$(l)Output$()$(li)Nothing below $(item)70 RPM$().$(li)Voltage: $(item)(RPM - 70) x 12$(), capped at $(item)10,000 V$().$(li)Power: $(item)(RPM - 70) x 320 W$().$(br2)At 256 RPM it gives $(item)2,232 V$() and $(item)59,520 W$(). The rotor has a stress impact of 240.

Take power from the $(item)stators$(). They handle 10,000 V, but most machines burn above $(item)1,000 V$(): run the line through insulators, cable tubes or posts into a $(item)large transformer$() before it reaches your factory.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
